title: Section 17 leave, CTOs and recall
blurb: Apply s17 leave rules, the CTO criteria and conditions, and the 72-hour recall and revocation process.
question: Marcus has been on a community treatment order for 4 months. He has missed two depot appointments, but his community nurse sees no sign of relapse or risk. His sister asks whether he will now be 'sent back to hospital'. What is the most accurate answer?

teach.h: Stepping out of hospital, still under the Act
teach.body: Section 17 leave lets a detained patient spend time out of hospital while still detained. A community treatment order (CTO, s17A) discharges a s3 patient from hospital but keeps them liable to recall. In plain English: leave is a short or trial absence with the section still running in hospital; a CTO is living in the community with conditions and a safety net.

teach.caption: Before granting leave of more than 7 consecutive days, the RC must first consider a CTO (s17(2A)-(2B)).

items: Only the responsible clinician can grant leave; nurses cannot grant it, but they check its terms before a patient goes out.
Leave can be indefinite, for specified occasions or a specified period, with conditions in the patient's interests or to protect others.
The RC can direct that the patient stays in custody (escorted leave) during the absence (s17(3)).
The RC can revoke leave by notice in writing if necessary for the patient's health or safety or to protect others (s17(4)).

head: Element
Requirement
rows: Nature or degree making medical treatment appropriate
For health, safety or protection of others
Treatment can be given without detention, subject to recall
RC needs the power to recall
Be available for examination for extension and for a SOAD
Set by RC with AMHP agreement: treatment, safety, protecting others

children.edge: Needs hospital treatment and risk of harm
children.label: Recall (s17E(1))
Review, not recall
children.sub: Breach may be taken into account

steps.label: CTO revoked
steps.sub: RC + AMHP agree s3 criteria met; s3 revives

teach.caption: If neither happens by 72 hours, the patient must be released and stays on the CTO. Revocation starts a new 6-month s3 period and an automatic tribunal referral.

teach.body: Taking his depot was a discretionary condition. Missing it does not by itself allow recall: the RC can recall only if Marcus needs hospital treatment and there would be a risk of harm without recall, or if he breaks a mandatory condition (s17E). The breach can be taken into account. His nurse arranges an urgent review, explores why he missed the depot (side effects?), and records the discussion. His sister is told recall is possible if those criteria are met.

teach.text: A CTO is NOT leave. A s2 patient can have s17 leave but cannot be put on a CTO, which needs s3 (or an unrestricted hospital order). And recall is NOT revocation: recall holds for up to 72 hours; revocation needs the AMHP's agreement and revives the s3.

items: s17 leave: RC only, with conditions; consider a CTO first for more than 7 consecutive days.
CTO: RC makes it for a s3 patient with an AMHP's written agreement; 6 months, 6 months, then yearly.
Recall: needs hospital treatment plus risk of harm, or breach of a mandatory condition; 72-hour maximum.
Revocation: RC and AMHP agree s3 criteria are met; s3 revives and the case is referred to the tribunal.

summary: You can now apply the rules on s17 leave, the criteria and conditions for a CTO, and the difference between recall and revocation. You can explain what a breach of a CTO condition does and does not allow.

A.q: Who can grant section 17 leave to a patient detained under section 3?
options: The nurse in charge of the ward
The hospital managers
The responsible clinician
The approved mental health professional
A.why: Section 17(1): the responsible clinician may grant leave of absence, subject to any conditions they consider necessary.

whyNot.0: Nurses carry out leave as agreed; they cannot grant it.
whyNot.1: Managers have discharge powers under s23 but do not grant leave.
whyNot.3: The AMHP's written agreement is needed for a CTO, not for leave.

A.q: How long does a community treatment order last before it must be extended?
options: 28 days
6 months
3 months
12 months
A.why: Section 20A(1): a CTO ceases after 6 months unless extended; it can then be extended for 6 months and then yearly.

whyNot.2: Three months is not a CTO period under the 1983 Act as in force.
whyNot.3: Yearly extensions apply only after the first 6-month extension.

A.q: For how long can a recalled CTO patient be held in hospital before they must be released or the CTO revoked?
options: 6 hours
28 days
24 hours
72 hours
A.why: Section 17F(6): if not released and the CTO not revoked by the end of 72 hours, the patient must be released, remaining on the CTO.

whyNot.0: 6 hours is the nurse's s5(4) holding power.

B.q: Ms Ade is detained under section 2. The team think she will do well at home and suggest a CTO. What is the correct position?
options: A CTO can be made with an AMHP's agreement
A CTO can be made after 14 days on s2
A CTO cannot be made from section 2
A CTO needs her nearest relative's consent
B.why: Section 17A(2): a CTO can be made for a patient detained under an application for admission for treatment (s3), not s2. She could have s17 leave instead.

whyNot.0: AMHP agreement is required, but the patient must be detained for treatment first.
whyNot.1: Time on s2 does not make a CTO available.
whyNot.3: The nearest relative's consent is not a statutory requirement for a CTO.

B.q: The RC plans to grant Mr Ford 10 consecutive days of leave to stay with his family. What must the RC do first?
options: Consider whether a CTO would be more suitable
Obtain an AMHP's written agreement to the leave
Seek a SOAD opinion on his medication
Refer the plan to the tribunal
B.why: Section 17(2A)-(2B): before granting longer-term leave (more than 7 consecutive days), the RC must first consider whether the patient should be dealt with under s17A instead.

whyNot.1: AMHP agreement is needed for a CTO, not for leave.
whyNot.2: A SOAD relates to Part 4 treatment safeguards, not leave.
whyNot.3: Tribunals review detention; they do not approve leave.

B.q: A CTO patient misses an appointment with the RC that was needed to examine him for extending the CTO. What does this allow?
options: Revocation of the CTO by the RC alone
Detention under section 5(2)
Recall for breach of a mandatory condition
Discharge from the CTO by the hospital managers
B.why: Section 17B(3)(a) makes availability for examination under s20A a mandatory condition, and s17E(2) allows recall if it is broken.

whyNot.0: Revocation needs the AMHP's written agreement and the s3 criteria.
whyNot.3: Missing an examination is not a reason for managers to discharge.

C.q: Marcus is on a CTO with a condition to accept his depot. He has missed two doses, but shows no relapse and there is no current risk of harm. Which action is most appropriate?
options: Issue a recall notice for breaching the condition
Review with him why the depot was missed
Ask police to take him to a place of safety
Revoke the CTO to restart section 3
C.why: Breaking a discretionary condition does not on its own allow recall (s17B(6)-(7)); recall needs the s17E(1) test. Reviewing the reasons, such as side effects, is the appropriate response.

whyNot.0: The s17E(1) test (needs hospital treatment and risk of harm) is not met here.
whyNot.2: Place-of-safety powers do not fit a person who is well and at home.
whyNot.3: Revocation follows recall and needs the s3 criteria to be met.

C.q: Jade, on a CTO, is recalled and arrives on the ward at 11:00 on Monday. The RC now believes she needs to stay for treatment. What must happen for the CTO to be revoked?
options: The nearest relative must be consulted and agree
Two doctors must complete new s3 recommendations
The tribunal must approve revocation
An AMHP must state in writing that they agree
C.why: Section 17F(4): the RC may revoke if the s3 conditions are met and an AMHP states in writing that they agree and it is appropriate. The s3 revives without a new application.

whyNot.0: The nearest relative's agreement is not a statutory condition of revocation.
whyNot.1: No new application or medical recommendations are needed; the s3 revives.
whyNot.2: The tribunal reviews afterwards through an automatic referral; it does not approve revocation.

C.q: Jade's CTO is not revoked and she has not been released by 11:00 on Thursday. What is her legal status?
options: She is detained under a revived section 3
She must be released and stays on the CTO
She is held under section 5(2) for 72 hours
She is fully discharged from the Act
C.why: Section 17F(6)-(7): at the end of 72 hours the patient must be released and remains subject to the CTO.

whyNot.0: A s3 revives only after revocation with AMHP agreement.
whyNot.2: Section 5(2) is for informal in-patients, not CTO patients (s5(6)).
whyNot.3: Release from recall does not end the CTO.

reteach.title: A lead, a long lead, and a pull back
reteach.question: How do leave, a CTO and recall fit together?

blocks.body: Leave: the patient is still detained and goes out on the RC's terms. CTO: the s3 patient is discharged to the community with conditions, and the RC can pull them back if needed. Recall: a short hold of up to 72 hours to decide whether they can go home again on the CTO or the CTO must be revoked, which brings back the s3.

blocks.text: Missing a depot is not, by itself, a ground for recall. Missing an examination for CTO extension or a SOAD certificate is.

explain.body: Granted by the RC, with conditions. Can be escorted (custody). Revocable by written notice if needed for health, safety or protection of others. Longer than 7 consecutive days: consider a CTO first.

test.q: How does the RC revoke a patient's section 17 leave?
options: By notice in writing
By phoning the ward
By applying to the managers
By asking the police to return them
test.why: Section 17(4): leave is revoked by notice in writing to the patient or the person in charge of them.

whyNot.3: Police may help return a patient, but revocation is the RC's written notice.

explain.body: The RC makes the order in writing for a s3 patient. An AMHP must state in writing that they agree the criteria are met and that it is appropriate. Conditions are set with the AMHP's agreement.

test.q: Which professional must agree in writing before a CTO can be made?
options: A second opinion doctor
The patient's GP
An AMHP
The community nurse
test.why: Section 17A(4)(b): an AMHP must state in writing that they agree with the RC and that it is appropriate to make the order.

whyNot.0: SOADs certify treatment under Part 4 and 4A, not the making of a CTO.
whyNot.1: The GP has no statutory role in making a CTO.
whyNot.3: The community nurse is consulted in practice but is not the statutory agreer.

explain.body: The RC recalls by written notice if the patient needs hospital treatment and there would be a risk of harm without recall, or if a mandatory condition is broken. The patient can be held for up to 72 hours.

test.q: Which is a lawful ground for recalling a CTO patient?
options: Missing one outpatient appointment
Needing hospital treatment with risk of harm
Moving to a new address
Their nearest relative asking the RC for recall
test.why: Section 17E(1): the patient requires treatment in hospital and there would be a risk of harm to health or safety or to others without recall.

whyNot.0: A routine missed appointment is not a statutory recall ground unless it is a mandatory examination.
whyNot.2: A change of address is not a recall ground.
whyNot.3: The nearest relative cannot trigger recall.

explain.body: During recall, the RC may revoke the CTO if the s3 criteria are met and an AMHP agrees in writing. The s3 revives with a new 6-month period, and managers refer the case to the tribunal as soon as possible.

test.q: After a CTO is revoked, what must the hospital managers do?
options: Hold a managers' hearing within 72 hours
Seek a new AMHP application
Inform the GP within 7 days
Refer the case to the tribunal
test.why: Section 68(7): managers must refer the case to the tribunal as soon as possible after a CTO is revoked.

whyNot.0: A managers' hearing is not required within 72 hours of revocation.
whyNot.1: No new application is needed; the s3 revives.
whyNot.2: Informing the GP is good practice but not the statutory duty here.
